titlePlain: Deployment Frequency, Lead Time, and the
subtitle: Lesson 1 · Platform Observability and Developer Experience

steps.label: Deployment Frequency
steps.sub: throughput — how often you ship to prod

steps.label: Lead Time for Changes
steps.sub: throughput — commit to running in prod

steps.label: Change Failure Rate
steps.sub: stability — % of deploys that degrade prod

code:
deployment_frequency  <- count of successful prod deploys
                          per day/week, from CI/CD or GitOps

lead_time_for_changes <- deploy_timestamp - commit_timestamp

change_failure_rate    <- failed_deploys / total_deploys

time_to_restore        <- incident_resolved_at
                           - incident_detected_at
caption: Pulled from systems you already run — commits, deploys, and tagged incidents.

steps.label: Elite
steps.sub: deploys on demand, multiple times a day

steps.label: High
steps.sub: deploys between once a day and once a week

steps.label: Medium
steps.sub: deploys between once a week and once a month

steps.label: Low
steps.sub: deploys less than once every six months

code:
# Throughput metrics and stability metrics
# are NOT a trade-off at elite performers:
#
#   high deployment frequency
#   + short lead time
#   + low change failure rate
#   + fast time to restore
#
# all four move together, not against each other
caption: Small changes, automated pipelines, and fast rollback improve speed and safety at once.

subtitle: The DORA metrics measure delivery. They don't measure whether developers can stand the platform.
